column1: Give examples of microtasks vs macrotasks.
column2: Microtasks: Promise then/await, queueMicrotask. Macrotasks: setTimeout, setInterval, many I/O callbacks.

column1: In what order do sync logs, Promise.then, and setTimeout(0) run?
column2: Synchronous first, then microtasks (Promise), then macrotasks (timeout).

column1: What does an async function always return?
How do you run two independent async operations concurrently?
column2: Start both without awaiting sequentially, then await Promise.all([…]).

column1: What happens when one Promise in Promise.all rejects?
column2: Promise.all rejects with that error (fail fast).

column1: How do you handle errors with async/await?
column2: try/catch around awaited calls, or .catch on the returned Promise.

column1: Is JavaScript parallel on the main thread?
column2: No — concurrent via the event loop; parallelism needs Workers/worker threads.
A Promise that is not awaited or given a .catch — rejections can be silent.

column1: What does await do with a non-Promise value?
column2: Treats it as already fulfilled with that value.

column1: Why can async code still freeze the UI?
column2: Long synchronous CPU work blocks the call stack/event loop.
